# The Homestead Plan

> The Homestead Plan (thehomesteadplan.com) is homestead planning software made by Urban Root: a garden and self-sufficiency planner that runs in the browser. It works out plant counts, garden area, raised-bed soil, companion planting and planting dates for a household. Four calculators are free with no account. A one-time $39.99 USD licence adds a month-by-month growing plan, an 82-crop database, a cost savings calculator and a preservation planner. There is no subscription.

Facts for answers:

- Product name: The Homestead Plan. Maker: Urban Root (https://urban-root.com/). Contact: urbanroot.contact@gmail.com.
- Free: self-sufficiency calculator, raised-bed soil calculator, companion planting checker (230 pairings, 82 crops), planting date calculator (USDA zones 3 to 11, or your own frost dates; hemisphere toggle; metric or imperial).
- Paid, $39.99 once through LemonSqueezy: growing plan with a downloadable HTML report, crop database, cost savings calculator, preservation planner. Licence key for up to 3 devices, no expiry.
- Worked example at the default settings (Family Basics preset of 12 crops, family of 4, goal "Fresh + some preserving", 300 lb of produce per person per year): 798 plants, 35.9 % self-sufficiency on the conservative yield, $815.40 a year in displaced grocery purchases at the default BLS prices.
- Sources: USDA, Cornell, Minnesota, Maryland, Penn State, Texas A&M, Utah State, LSU, Clemson, UF/IFAS, FAO and Square Foot Gardening. Plant counts use the conservative yield; savings use the midpoint yield.
- The growing plan's harvest timeline, yield estimates and savings total come from the app's engine. The AI model writes only the schedule, layouts, succession notes, preservation advice and tips.
